title: The Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse Architecture now supports Tag-Based Access Control for federated catalogs
key_points: Lake Formation tag-based access control now covers federated catalogs too, so the same LF-Tags govern S3 Tables, Redshift and external sources such as DynamoDB, Snowflake or BigQuery.
Permissions follow the tags, so new tables inherit access without editing grants; a data steward creates tags and grants by domain and sensitivity.
Walkthrough checks the result as different roles from Athena, the Redshift query editor and EMR.
services: AWS Lake Formation, Amazon SageMaker Lakehouse, Amazon S3 Tables, Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena, Amazon EMR, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: Per-resource grants vs tag-based access control across lake and warehouse catalogs
authors: Sandeep Adwankar, Aarthi Srinivasan, Srividya Parthasarathy

title: Modernize Amazon Redshift authentication by migrating user management to AWS IAM Identity Center
key_points: An open-source utility from AWS reads a Redshift warehouse's local users, groups and roles, creates matching users and groups in IAM Identity Center, and recreates the grants on new Identity Center roles inside Redshift.
Grants made directly to individual users must first be moved onto roles; Lake Formation permissions and connecting the identity provider are outside its scope.
A prerequisite for trusted identity propagation, where the same signed-in user flows from Redshift to other analytics services.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Serverless, AWS IAM Identity Center
decision: Local database users and groups vs Identity Center users with trusted identity propagation for Redshift access management
authors: Ziad Wali, Maneesh Sharma, Satesh Sonti, Sumanth Punyamurthula

title: Implement fine-grained access control using Amazon OpenSearch Service and JSON Web Tokens
key_points: Users log in through Cognito, and the JWT's group claims map to OpenSearch roles that limit which documents and fields each user can see.
Four scenarios show different roles getting different search results; search-application security, not data engineering.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon Cognito, AWS Lambda
authors: Ramya Bhat, Shubhansu Sawaria, Soujanya Konka

title: How Ancestry optimizes a 100-billion-row Iceberg table
key_points: AWS reports Ancestry's hints table holds about 100 billion rows with around 7 million changes an hour, merged hourly by Spark on EMR on EC2, and that the tuning cut cost by 75%.

The levers: partition by the columns queries filter on, sort within partitions on a truncated ID, merge-on-read instead of copy-on-write, compaction with high concurrency and partial progress that also rewrites delete files, and regular snapshot expiry.

Merges avoid shuffles with storage-partitioned joins and by bounding the target to the batch's ID range; the post notes that the Glue table optimizer is enough for most tables and custom maintenance is only for extreme cases.
services: Apache Iceberg, Amazon EMR, Apache Spark, Amazon S3, AWS Glue Data Catalog
decision: Merge-on-read vs copy-on-write, and managed table optimizer vs custom compaction, for a very large Iceberg table with frequent merges
authors: Ancestry — Thomas Cardenas, Robert Fisher, Harsh Vardhan Singh Gaur

title: How AppZen enhances operational efficiency, scalability, and security with Amazon OpenSearch Serverless
key_points: AppZen moved central logging for many accounts from self-managed Elasticsearch to OpenSearch Serverless, fed by OpenSearch Ingestion pipelines.
Capacity was sized by ingesting in parallel to both systems before cutover; also covers index strategy and cost tuning. Log analytics, off the reader's path.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, AWS Organizations
authors: AppZen — Prashanth Dudipala, Madhuri Andhale, Manoj Gupta, Prashant Agrawal

title: Best practices for migrating Teradata BTEQ scripts to Amazon Redshift RSQL
key_points: Schema Conversion Tool translates BTEQ syntax to RSQL, but the output still needs work to be production-ready; the post lists what to add by hand.

Practices include environment parameter files, temporary IAM credentials, echoing queries to logs, step-numbered exit codes to locate failures, query groups and search paths, and folding several UPDATEs into one INSERT.
Ends with a script skeleton that combines these, useful for Teradata-to-Redshift migration engagements.
services: Amazon Redshift, Amazon Redshift RSQL, AWS Schema Conversion Tool, Teradata
decision: Keep converted BTEQ logic as RSQL shell scripts vs rewrite it as stored procedures or dbt models when moving from Teradata
authors: Ankur Bhanawat, Raj Patel

title: Amazon Redshift Serverless at 4 RPUs: High-value analytics at low cost
key_points: Redshift Serverless gets a smaller minimum base capacity; AWS reports 4 RPUs with 64 GB of memory, a 32 TB managed-storage cap and up to 100 columns per table, at about USD 1.50 per active hour in us-east-1.

Aimed at dev/test, CI runs, departmental marts and data-quality jobs; a catch is that once a workgroup scales above the base it keeps the higher level, and AWS reports a 60-second minimum charge per query, so short queries should be batched.
Cost controls repeat the usual list: RPU-hour usage limits, tracking consumption in SYS_SERVERLESS_USAGE and closing idle transactions.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift Serverless
decision: Smallest Serverless base capacity vs a larger base vs provisioned for dev/test and small, bursty warehouse workloads
attaches_to: dbt-pipelines (run the NYC 311 dbt build on the smallest vs default base capacity and compare runtime and cost)
authors: Ricardo Serafim, Ashish Agrawal, Andre Hass

title: Amazon SageMaker Catalog expands discoverability and governance for Amazon S3 general purpose buckets
key_points: Ordinary S3 buckets and prefixes, including unstructured files such as documents and images, can now be published as SageMaker Catalog assets, not only S3 Tables.
Consumers find the asset and request access; once the producer approves, access is granted through S3 Access Grants, so discovery and S3 permissions become one workflow instead of two.
Relevant when governance work reaches raw files that never become tables.
services: Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon S3, S3 Access Grants
decision: Catalog subscription with S3 Access Grants vs hand-written bucket policies for sharing raw S3 prefixes across teams
authors: Priya Tiruthani, Yuhang Huang, Santhosh Padmanabhan, Subrat Das

title: Zeta reduces banking incident response time by 80% with Amazon OpenSearch Service observability
key_points: Zeta, a core-banking SaaS provider, built tenant-aware monitoring on OpenSearch that collects AWS resource logs, application logs and distributed traces, with hot, warm and cold storage tiers to control cost.
AWS reports an 80% faster incident response; the content is observability platform design, outside the reader's data-engineering path.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion
authors: Zeta — Deepesh Dhapola, Tarun Chakraborty, Hitesh Subnani, Shashidhar Soppin, Manochandra Menni, Anchal Kansal

title: Build enterprise-scale log ingestion pipelines with Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: Lays out the layers of a log pipeline (collect, buffer, process, store) and the usual ingestion choices: log shippers, Firehose, Lambda or OpenSearch Ingestion.
Deploys an OpenSearch Ingestion example with index templates and gives operational tips on sizing, buffering and retention; log analytics rather than data platform work.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service, Amazon OpenSearch Ingestion, Amazon Data Firehose, AWS Lambda
authors: Akhil B, Ramya Bhat, Chanpreet Singh

title: Improve Amazon EMR HBase availability and tail latency using generational ZGC
key_points: EMR 7.10 lets HBase RegionServers run the generational Z garbage collector, which keeps GC pauses very short and so cuts tail-latency spikes.
Adds tuning advice: fixed heap size, pre-touching memory and raising memory-map limits, plus BucketCache changes.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache HBase
authors: Vishal Chaudhary, Ramesh Kandasamy

title: Guide to adopting Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio from ATPCO’s Journey
key_points: ATPCO, an airline-pricing data provider, already governed data with DataZone and moved to SageMaker Unified Studio, organising users into domain units (data engineering, analysts, sales) with a project per team.
The walkthrough onboards existing S3 data, an existing Glue Data Catalog and Redshift tables into those projects, then shows analysts working across them from notebooks and the SQL editor.
Useful only as an example of how domain units map to an organisation; most of the post is console setup.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog, Amazon DataZone, AWS Glue Data Catalog, Amazon Redshift, Amazon S3
decision: Domain units per business function vs one flat set of projects for governing a shared analytics platform
authors: ATPCO — Mitesh Patel, Nikki Rouda, Raj Samineni, Saurabh Rawat

title: Achieve low-latency data processing with Amazon EMR on AWS Local Zones
key_points: Runs an EMR cluster with Flink in an AWS Local Zone near corporate offices to inspect network traffic for a secure web gateway, with Kafka on EKS queuing requests and streaming rule updates.
Covers which instance types and services are available in Local Zones and how to launch EMR there; an edge security use case far from analytics pipelines.
services: Amazon EMR, Apache Flink, AWS Local Zones, Amazon EKS, Apache Kafka, Amazon S3
authors: Gagan Brahmi, Arun Shanmugam, George Oakes

title: Export JMX metrics from Kafka connectors in Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka Connect with a custom plugin
key_points: MSK Connect sends only worker-level metrics to CloudWatch; the connector's own JMX metrics (for example Debezium's replication lag and snapshot progress) stay inside the JVM.

The fix packages a small extra Java module next to the unmodified Debezium MySQL connector in the custom plugin; the module reads the MBeans and publishes them as CloudWatch custom metrics, so the connector can be upgraded without re-patching.
Worth knowing for CDC monitoring, but it is Java packaging work rather than a data design choice.
services: Amazon MSK, Amazon MSK Connect, Debezium, Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon Aurora MySQL
decision: Built-in MSK Connect metrics vs wrapper module exporting connector JMX metrics vs patched connector code for CDC connector monitoring
authors: Jaydev Nath, David John Chakram, Sharmila Shanmugam

title: Enhance Amazon EMR observability with automated incident mitigation using Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Managed Grafana
key_points: EMR cluster metrics flow to Managed Prometheus and Grafana; alert rules notify through SNS and trigger Systems Manager scripts for first-aid fixes.
A Bedrock agent with a knowledge base of past incidents and support articles suggests what to do next for each alert.
Deployed with CloudFormation and tested with an HBase RegionServer failure and a CPU stress test.
services: Amazon EMR, Amazon Managed Grafana, Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, Amazon Bedrock, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS
decision: Manual runbooks vs alert-triggered automated first aid plus AI-suggested fixes for cluster incidents
authors: Yu-Ting Su

title: Cluster manager communication simplified with Remote Publication
key_points: OpenSearch's elected cluster manager now writes cluster state to a remote store and followers download it, instead of pushing the full state over the transport layer to every node.

AWS reports this is one of the changes behind domains of up to 1,000 nodes and 500,000 shards, and it keeps metadata safe even if most cluster manager nodes are lost; internals only, nothing to build.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service
authors: Himshikha Gupta, Sooraj Sinha

title: Integrate scientific data management and analytics with the next generation of Amazon SageMaker, Part 1
key_points: Life-sciences scenario in SageMaker Unified Studio: one research team publishes datasets to the catalog, another finds them, requests access and analyses them once the producer approves.
Standard publish-subscribe catalog flow told for scientists; no new technical content.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon SageMaker Catalog
authors: Nadeem Bulsara, Chaitanya Vejendla, Chris Clark, Nick Furr, Mileidy Giraldo, Subrat Das

title: Build a multi-tenant healthcare system with Amazon OpenSearch Service
key_points: Design guide for serving hospital departments, clinics, insurers and researchers from shared OpenSearch infrastructure: isolation models, per-tenant workload limits, fine-grained security and storage tiers for retention.
Search-platform multi-tenancy; nothing for the reader's data pipelines.
services: Amazon OpenSearch Service
authors: Ezat Karimi, Jon Handler

title: Near real-time streaming analytics on protobuf with Amazon Redshift
key_points: Redshift streaming ingestion reads binary protobuf messages from MSK or Kinesis into an auto-refreshing materialized view, and a Lambda UDF decodes each message to JSON stored as SUPER.
Because Lambda cannot take raw binary, the view hex-encodes the payload first; the decoder needs the protobuf library and generated classes in a Lambda layer.
Suggests adding Glue Schema Registry for schema changes; a compact build the reader can redo with Kinesis on Redshift Serverless and measure ingest lag and Lambda cost.
services: Amazon Redshift, Redshift streaming ingestion, AWS Lambda, Amazon MSK, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, Redshift SUPER / PartiQL
decision: Decode binary events inside Redshift via a Lambda UDF vs upstream in a stream processor vs in Firehose before landing
attaches_to: aws-bytes: real-time streaming (later); dbt-pipelines (SUPER landing on Redshift Serverless)
authors: Konstantinos Tzouvanas, John Mousa, Marios Parthenios, Pavlos Kaimakis

title: Develop and deploy a generative AI application using Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
key_points: Builds a news-and-sentiment assistant for financial analysts with Bedrock Flows inside a SageMaker Unified Studio project, then tests it in the studio.
Low-code GenAI app tutorial; no data engineering or data platform content.
services: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio, Amazon Bedrock Flows, Amazon Bedrock
authors: Amit Maindola, Arghya Banerjee, Melody Yang, Gaurav Parekh
